themes_detail.label: Plumbing Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints in CD 206 spiked to 3 reports this week, a 500% surge over the 8-week baseline average of 0.5 complaints per week (z-score: 3.54), suggesting a possible widespread system failure or contamination event affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 3 plumbing complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase, z-score 3.54)
Plumbing ranks 6th among all 311 complaint types over 90 days with 559 total complaints, indicating chronic baseline issue
Spike is statistically significant and sudden, not a gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview residents in affected buildings to identify common symptoms (water discoloration, pressure loss, backups)
Contact DEP to determine if aging infrastructure in Belmont/East Tremont contributed to this week's spike

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Alarm Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints exploded 1500% two weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score: 8.66), the largest statistical spike in the district's data, though no recent follow-up reports suggest the acute event may have passed.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike, highest z-score of 8.66 in dataset)
No air quality complaints reported in current week, suggesting acute event has resolved or abated
Timing suggests potential industrial emission, traffic event, or weather-driven air stagnation episode
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the air quality spike two weeks ago—check for industrial incidents, construction, or traffic anomalies
Interview residents who filed complaints about specific symptoms (odors, respiratory issues, visibility)

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge Two Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked 647% two weeks ago (14 complaints vs. 1.9 weekly average, z-score: 5.98), representing a significant sudden increase in homelessness visibility, though current week data is unavailable to assess persistence.
evidence: 14 encampment complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (647% increase, z-score 5.98)
Second-highest statistical spike in dataset after air quality, indicating major concentrated event
No Reddit discussions or recent news coverage available to contextualize whether spike persists
reporting_angles: Map the 14 encampment complaints to identify hotspot neighborhoods within Belmont/East Tremont
Interview outreach workers and DSS to understand whether two-week spike reflects new arrivals, seasonal pattern, or service gaps

themes_detail.label: Consumer Complaints Climb
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints in CD 206 rose 167% two weeks ago (9 complaints vs. 3.4 weekly average, z-score: 3.76), suggesting possible fraud, predatory business practices, or scams targeting vulnerable residents in the district.
evidence: 9 consumer complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (167% increase, z-score 3.76)
Type of consumer complaints undefined in data; requires follow-up to identify specific scams or problematic vendors
Spike is recent but details are opaque without access to complaint text or categories
reporting_angles: Request DCA complaint summaries to identify whether spike stems from one industry (utilities, telecom, repair services) or scattered fraud
Interview AARP and senior centers about whether vulnerable elderly residents are being targeted

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Rising Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints (residential + street/sidewalk combined) increased 70% last week (10 complaints vs. 5.9 weekly average, z-score: 3.03), consistent with heat season displacement and increased outdoor activity, though still well below the 2,508 total noise complaints over 90 days.
evidence: 10 noise complaints filed last week vs. 5.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (70% increase, z-score 3.03)
Noise is the #1 complaint category district-wide (1,890 residential noise complaints over 90 days), indicating endemic problem
Seasonal spike likely reflects warmer weather and outdoor gathering; pattern consistent with prior years
reporting_angles: Interview residents about which specific noise sources dominate (bars, construction, traffic, street vendors)
Assess whether NYPD noise enforcement has been deployed or whether community relations have deteriorated
